summary: A checkpoint copies committed transactions from the -wal file back into the main database file. By default SQLite runs a PASSIVE auto-checkpoint when a COMMIT pushes the WAL past 1000 pages, and when the last connection closes. Applications can disable auto-checkpoints and checkpoint explicitly with PRAGMA wal_checkpoint or sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2 in PASSIVE, FULL, RESTART, or TRUNCATE mode. Checkpointing matters because the WAL is only rewound after a checkpoint reaches its end while no reader still uses it. Long-lived or overlapping read transactions, and statements that are never reset, cause checkpoint starvation and unbounded WAL growth. The experimental wal2 branch targets the continuous-writer case.

claims.text: By default SQLite auto-checkpoints when a COMMIT leaves the WAL at 1000 pages or more, and when the last connection closes; the threshold is changeable via PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT.
Auto-checkpoints are PASSIVE: they copy as many frames as possible without waiting and never invoke the busy handler, so they can make little progress under contention.

FULL waits (via busy handler) for writers to finish and readers to reach the latest snapshot, then checkpoints all frames; RESTART additionally waits until readers no longer use the WAL so the next writer rewinds it; TRUNCATE additionally truncates the WAL to zero bytes. These modes block new writers but not new readers while waiting.

If the busy handler gives up during FULL/RESTART/TRUNCATE, the call degrades to PASSIVE behaviour and returns SQLITE_BUSY; a concurrent checkpoint in another connection returns SQLITE_BUSY immediately.
A normal checkpoint does not shrink the WAL file; the file is rewound and overwritten from the start unless journal_size_limit is set or a TRUNCATE checkpoint runs.

Checkpoint starvation: if at least one read transaction is always open, checkpoints never reach the end of the WAL and the WAL grows without bound; fixes are reader gaps or periodic RESTART/TRUNCATE checkpoints.

A prepared statement that is stepped but never reset or finalized keeps its transaction open and is a common cause of a WAL that never shrinks; forcing PRAGMA wal_checkpoint and checking file size diagnoses it.
Operators under heavy load pair default auto-checkpoints with a separate maintenance task that checks WAL size and issues TRUNCATE checkpoints.
The wal2 branch alternates between two WAL files so continuous writers no longer cause unbounded growth, but long-running readers can still prevent full checkpoints; it is not in mainline SQLite.

disagreements.text: Secondary tutorials disagree on whether RESTART blocks readers; the official API doc says it blocks new writers, not readers, but waits on existing readers.

open_questions: Whether wal2 or begin-concurrent will merge into mainline SQLite.
